info.name: IMS — Suppliers, Items and PO Creation
info.description: Source-based illustrative examples. Supplier endpoints are public; everything else needs a bearer token. Set base_url, token, supplier_id, lookupcode, transfer_request_id, item_hq_id and purchase_order_id. PO workflow: create transfer -> add items (single or bulk) -> create order -> PO conditions -> commit (isClosed 0 for each partial shipment, 1 to close). Validation returns only the first error.

request.description: Creates an open transfer request, not the final purchase order. type must be exactly PO. supplier_id is required integer Supplier.ID. other_store_id is optional for PO; omit it. store_id comes from the token user. Optional title (string max 255); omit to use the server-generated title. Optional delivery_date must be a date today or later; omit when unused, not null. Response type is the integer 0 for PO. items is omitted on creation. Use the returned id as transfer_request_id, add items, then create order. The default title uses the PO supplier and store names. Response type is a JSON integer: 0=PO, 1=HQ PO, 2=TransferIN, 4=HQ TransferIN; 3/5 are TransferOut or ReturnToSupplier, distinguished by other-store versus supplier IDs.

request.description: Prerequisite for creating an order. id is Item.HQID, matching supplier-item search data.id; it is not supplier-details items[].id. quantity is required numeric; current rules do not enforce a positive minimum. notes is optional nullable string max 1000. Existing items are updated, otherwise added. No supplier-item membership validation is implemented here. Response type is a JSON integer: 0=PO, 1=HQ PO, 2=TransferIN, 4=HQ TransferIN; 3/5 are TransferOut or ReturnToSupplier, distinguished by other-store versus supplier IDs.

request.description: Adds or updates several items at once. Each id is an Item HQID. Every id is saved with quantity 1: new ones are added, ones already on the transfer request are reset to 1. Other items on the request are not removed. Validation: ids required, non-empty array, distinct, each must exist in Item.HQID. Returns the saved items. Response type is a JSON integer: 0=PO, 1=HQ PO, 2=TransferIN, 4=HQ TransferIN; 3/5 are TransferOut or ReturnToSupplier, distinguished by other-store versus supplier IDs.

request.description: Creates the actual order from the stored transfer type, supplier and items. No request body. Requires existing items and a cashier on the token user. PO / ReturnToSupplier send SupplierID with OtherStoreID=0 and save the downstream id as purchase_order_id. TransferIN schedules a sync job that fills purchase_order_id later. On success the transfer request is closed. Response type is a JSON integer: 0=PO, 1=HQ PO, 2=TransferIN, 4=HQ TransferIN; 3/5 are TransferOut or ReturnToSupplier, distinguished by other-store versus supplier IDs.

request.description:
Commits a purchase order. The flow is picked by the order's POType, not by the body:
- 0 ReturnToSupplier: no body fields. Always closes via /api/commit-order.
- 1 PO: isClosed required (0|1). 1 closes via /api/commit-order, 0 receives a partial batch via /api/partial-po.
- 2/4 TransferIN: isClosed required (0|1) and Vehicle_tempIN (or vehicle_TempIN) required. 1 closes via /api/commit-order, 0 is partial via /api/partial-transfer-in and may carry the delivery conditions.
- 3/5 TransferOut: VehicleType and seal_number required, other condition fields optional. Always closes.
After every successful commit (partial included) a PDF -> email -> print chain runs. Errors from the order service keep their status (4xx) with its message; server failures are 500, unreachable is 502.

- 2/4 TransferIN: isClosed required (0|1) and Vehicle_tempIN (or vehicle_TempIN) required. 1 closes via /api/commit-order, 0 is partial via /api/partial-transfer-in and may carry the delivery conditions.
- 3/5 TransferOut: VehicleType and seal_number required, other condition fields optional. Always closes.
After every successful commit (partial included) a PDF -> email -> print chain runs. Errors from the order service keep their status (4xx) with its message; server failures are 500, unreachable is 502.

request.description: Requires bearer token. Matches ItemLookupCode LIKE lookup%, returning the first matching item without an explicit sort. This is a prefix lookup, not an exact search; aliases are not searched. SQL LIKE wildcards in the input are not escaped. No active/HQID filter is applied. Success data.id is Item.HQID. Current implementation does not handle no match: ShowItemResource accesses a null model, causing a 500 instead of an Item not found 404. Saved missing-item example assumes APP_DEBUG=false; debug=true exposes the exception message and trace. Response type is a JSON integer: 0=PO, 1=HQ PO, 2=TransferIN, 4=HQ TransferIN; 3/5 are TransferOut or ReturnToSupplier, distinguished by other-store versus supplier IDs.
